title: dedicated-autoscaler-throughput-burst-controls-and-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Enhances Dedicated autoscaler with configurable throughput guarantees, smoother burst controls, and improved utilization reporting. Includes metrics and dashboards for ops and a migration path. No API changes for customers.
description: Context: customers operating Dedicated fleets reported two issues under high tail loads: (1) unpredictable throughput drop when many short-lived requests arrive (burst patterns), and (2) lack of visibility into token-bucket throttles and backpressure events. This PR implements a combined approach: add a throughput-guarantee mode for reserved pools, introduce a smoothing layer on the token-bucket burst allowance to avoid sharp throttles, and expand utilization reporting to surface burst/queueing metrics in the Console. Motivation: reduce P99 latency spikes and provide ops better signals to tune autoscaler policies.Major changes: (1) autoscaler/controller: new throughputGuarantee config and enforcement path; (2) tokenbucket/smoother: implements moving-average smoothing with configurable window and max-burst cap; (3) reporting: emit dedicated.autoscaler.burst_allowed, dedicated.autoscaler.burst_throttled, dedicated.autoscaler.queue_depth and dedicate.fleet.utilization percentiles; (4) docs and runbook updates for ops and migration; (5) tests and perf harness updates to validate behavior.Backwards compatibility: all new behavior is behind a feature flag defaulted to off for existing fleets. Customers can opt in per-fleet by setting dedicated.autoscaler.throughputGuarantee.enabled=true in the Dedicated CRD.Migration: add flag to Dedicated values.yaml or use Console toggle, then gradually enable on small fleets to monitor metrics.Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-4234) - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Perf benchmarks and before/after metrics - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] Feature flag gating and safe defaultsTesting and results: microbench harness simulating short-lived requests (mean size 128 tokens) across 3 fleet sizes. Results: steady-state throughput improved by ~9-14% for 95th-percentile latency SLOs and P99 latency reduced by ~18% under burst traffic. Token-bucket smoothing reduced throttle oscillations by ~60%. Observability: new Grafana dashboard panels and alert rule suggestions included. CI: initial run showed a flaky e2e related to a test harness timeout (fixed by increasing harness timeout and retry logic).Notes for ops: enable feature flag on non-critical fleet, monitor dedicated.autoscaler.burst_throttled and dedicated.fleet.utilization. Tweak smoothing.window_ms (default 500ms) and smoothing.max_burst_tokens per GPU type. Follow runbook if queue_depth grows > 5x baseline.Related: ENG-4234 design doc, ENG-4370 rollout plan, SUP-912 customer incident that prompted this work.

perf_results: P99 latency: reduced from 310ms to 254ms (-18%) under burst profile
Throttle oscillation metric: variance reduced by ~60%
notes_for_ops: Recommended rollout: enable on canary fleet, observe dedicated.autoscaler.burst_throttled and dedicated.fleet.utilization for 24h
Tunable params: smoothing.window_ms (default 500), smoothing.max_burst_tokens (default per-GPU), throughputGuarantee.min_reserved_rps
If queue_depth increases >5x baseline, rollback flag and follow runbook ops/dedicated-autoscaler.md#rollback
